fieldsRead.text: Automotive Technology at TU/e is a major within the Electrical Engineering bachelor. This English-taught programme studies cars as integrated systems, combining electronics, software, sensing and control with vehicle dynamics, propulsion and energy conversion. Design challenges and a final bachelor project develop the application of these fields.

The first UCR programme develops mathematical and computational methods for autonomous and connected systems. The second combines intelligent-system methods with sustainable energy and product assessment. These are related academic responses: neither supplies the specialist circuits, embedded hardware, vehicle dynamics, propulsion and power-electronics formation of the TU/e major.
Automotive Technology major within the Electrical Engineering BSc

The 45 EC of electives remain open, subject to level, prior-knowledge, overlap and approval rules. The 10-EC final project requires 120 EC including all required first-year components. Five Studium Generale activities and MyFuture activities totalling value seven are additional non-credit requirements.

Study autonomous and connected systems through mathematical models, programming, data analysis, computer vision, robot motion, learning agents and communication networks. Product design and life-cycle analysis connect these methods to practical system choices. Mobility is an application of these methods; vehicle hardware and propulsion are not taught as a specialist sequence.

Combine mathematical models, perception, robot motion and intelligent decisions with renewable-energy conversion and system design, life-cycle assessment and material recovery. The programme examines how intelligent products and their energy and material systems can be designed and evaluated. It offers methods relevant to lower-impact mobility, without specialist vehicle powertrain or battery engineering.
